H1.note: MEIS1 arm from where the chain starts (the rs113851554 T allele); BTBD9 arm from 'loss of BTBD9' (H1.4). The title's BTBD9 risk alleles appear in no H1 step.

H2.note: 'dysfunction reproduces the brain-iron-deficiency state'. BTBD9 is listed in H2's genes, but no H2 step names it and no direction is given.

H3.no_claim_reason: no direction: PTPRD risk alleles 'alter' the E/I synapse balance, and the run itself says allele directions at PTPRD are mixed

H4.no_claim_reason: a null claim: GABARAPL2 and GLIPR1 are passengers with no causal role; not a signed effect

H5.note: 'BTBD9 hypofunction'; the chain starts at BTBD9. Its last step is about the rs10947738 allele, which no claim starts from. ACO1 and MEIS1 are listed as genes but get no direction toward RLS.

findings.detail: H1.2 ends at 'inhibition of cerebellar output' and nothing continues from it; H1.3 restarts at 'loss of MEIS1', so the cerebellar branch never reaches sleep, movement or RLS.

H1.3 ends at 'abnormal circadian sleep/wake cycle' and H1.4 restarts at 'loss of BTBD9', so the MEIS1 sleep branch dead-ends; only H1.4's 'abnormal sleep behavior' continues, as the sleep half of H1.5's 'abnormal sleep/motor output'.
Neither the GWAS row nor the OT score says the rs113851554 T allele lowers MEIS1; the run's own note admits the direction is inferred from mouse loss-of-function models.

The run's strongest datum (rs113851554-T with RLS, p = 1e-1371) supports variant-to-RLS directly, but no step states that; it is cited only for an expression effect it does not show. I did not bridge it, as it would replace the whole chain.

The RLS disease-model annotations (AGR DOID:0050425 for Meis1 and Btbd9) are cited at phenotype steps they do not state; at H2.2 the Aco1 tm1Roua 'abnormal iron homeostasis' annotation gives no direction on iron homeostasis itself.

The kept MGI records name genotypes (Meis1 em1Rihw, Btbd9 tm1c with Pcp2-cre, Btbd9 Gt(RRE078)Byg) without saying they are losses, and the H1 mechanism calls the Purkinje-cell conditional Btbd9 genotype a 'null'; the inversion to 'loss of X' rests on the run's reading of allele names.
The mechanism says 'MEIS1 loss disinhibits cerebellar output'; the cited paper is zebrafish meis1b mutants, which the run never says.
The Btbd9 sleep annotation is for a Pcp2-cre conditional genotype (named in the record), which would bear on H1's cerebellar story; the run does not use it.

H1.5 is H1's only link to RLS, and its one text says sleep disruption and periodic limb movements are features (consequences) of RLS; the chain uses them as the final causal link, so the BTBD9 route of H1 and H5 (S4 then S5) composes a consequence of RLS as its cause.

PMID:17634447 reports the BTBD9 risk variant lowers serum ferritin 13% per allele: direct evidence for H5's BTBD9-iron convergence and H2's iron axis, yet it is cited only for the sleep/motor association, and no step states the ferritin result.

'high' and 'grounded', but only one junction connects (H1.4 to H1.5); the MEIS1 arm has no route, the H1.1 expression effect has no support, the mouse records do not state the allele type, the circuit evidence is zebrafish, and the RLS link is a disease feature.

H2.2 ends at 'iron homeostasis' (a process), H2.3 starts at 'brain iron deficiency' (an amount in brain), and H2.3 ends at 'RLS-like motor behaviour' while H2.4 starts at 'iron repletion'; ACO1 never reaches brain iron or RLS.
An efficacy arrow (iron repletion inhibits RLS) rests on a trial registry record with status only; the run's note says so but keeps the arrow.
AGR:MGI:87879:MP:0020369 is a ROSA26 Aco1* transgene raising intestinal iron, a gain-type genotype; it cannot show ACO1 is required for iron homeostasis.

OT:ACO1-MONDO_0005391 (0.23), OT:ACO1-constraint, PMID:21226925 and AGR:MGI:1916625:MP:0005266 (H5's) are listed as support but state no H2 step; no step links ACO1 to RLS at all. OT:ACO1-tractability states H2.1 only by repeating P21399's text.
PMID:21226925 is a systems-biology network study of 124 diseases; its text names neither RLS, ACO1 nor iron.
'medium' though no step connects ACO1 to brain iron or RLS, its own contradicting note says GWAS Catalog has no ACO1 variant, and the BTBD9 link in the mechanism rests on one STRING edge.
BTBD9 is listed among H2's genes but appears in no H2 step.
PMID:40561837's corpus callosum result is an MR path from RLS to ADHD, not a PTPRD association; the step fuses it with the PTPRD pleiotropy finding.
Steps cite Reactome and STRING over-representation results with one matched gene (FDR 0.04-0.08) as if they showed function; for H4.2 the run's own note calls them single-gene artefacts.

R-HSA-388844 (enrichment) and AGR:MGI:97812:MP:0001522 (Ptprd null, impaired swimming) are listed as support but state no step; the run's own contradicting note says the mouse does not support an RLS readout.
The contradicting note names rs4596705 (beta decrease), which is not in the run's sources.
H4.3 (MEIS1, PTPRD, BTBD9 with RLS) cites only an enrichment and two text-mined edges, though the run held direct GWAS rows and PMID:17637780 for each gene; I moved those in.
GLIPR1 is in H4's title and genes but in no step; its only records (P48060, OT tractability and constraint) state nothing about RLS.
'GABARAPL2 homozygous mouse null is preweaning lethal' and 'GLIPR1 is blood-vessel-enriched' have no source in the run.

R-HSA-1989781, P48060, OT:GLIPR1-tractability, OT:GABARAPL2-constraint and OT:GLIPR1-constraint state no step (OT:GABARAPL2-tractability states H4.1 only by repeating P60520's text); the tractability records' 'associatedDiseases.count: 0' is the only datum for the null claim, and no step carries it.
BTBD9 lowering ACO1 is the hypothesis itself; the cited UniProt entry says 'No curated function statement'. The run says so and rates H5 low, which is fair.
H5.2 ends at ACO1 and nothing in the run takes ACO1 amount anywhere; H5.3 restarts at 'loss of BTBD9' and H5.5 at a variant, so the convergence never reaches RLS.
Most process and phenotype nodes have empty CURIEs and grounding_evidence, and RLS is written 'EFO:MONDO_0005391', which is not a valid CURIE.

H5 says BTBD9 lowers ACO1 (H5.2) and its falsification predicts more IRP1 when BTBD9 is lost, while H2 says ACO1 loss causes RLS; composed, BTBD9 loss would raise ACO1 and lower RLS risk, the opposite of H5's 'BTBD9 hypofunction' and of the H1/H2 'two outputs of one node' it claims to unify.

'the only gene in this set with strong brain expression, highest in excitatory and inhibitory neurons' (and H3.2's context) has no source: P23468 says only 'neurons', and the run cites no expression record.
Every hypothesis gives contradicting evidence as prose with no accession, and sources.json has no 'contradicting' entries, so none of it can be attached as refuting evidence.
BLN:CerebellarOutputInhibition: no GO, MP or HP term for inhibitory control of the cerebellum's output (only development and morphology terms).
SO:0001182 iron_responsive_element must be declared kind 'variant' because render maps every SO term to variant; an IRE is an RNA sequence feature, not a variant.

The guide says 'MP for a mouse phenotype' but statements are species-agnostic, so the choice of MP or HP decides whether chains connect; H1.4's 'abnormal sleep behavior' and H1.5's sleep half are one node on HP:0002360 (taxon on the evidence), while the narrower MP:0020478 stays separate. A uPheno-style rule would settle this.
A model-organism disease-model annotation ('genotype X is a model of RLS') has no statement form, and its allele type is not in the record, so it cannot be an effect.

The guide treats 'loss of X leads to abnormal Y' as an effect on an 'abnormal Y' term, but lists MGI 'abnormal Y' annotations as no_direction without saying that applies only when the step's target is Y itself (H2.2), not the abnormal-Y term (H1.3, H5.3); and whether the annotated allele is a loss is recorded only in MGI nomenclature.

An assoc with a disease target must take a risk/severity/progression aspect; a disease feature (sleep disruption caused by RLS) fits none, and if a route reached it fromAssoc would compose a consequence of RLS as a cause of it.
Comorbidity (two diseases together, 'ADHD-RLS comorbidity') has no target form.
A null claim ('GABARAPL2 and GLIPR1 are not drivers', OT associatedDiseases.count 0) cannot be stated; 'none' means unsigned, not absent.
Open Targets association scores have no evidence kind; I used observational because the score is mostly genetic association.
OT scores re-count the GWAS rows kept beside them, and rs9296249 is from the same study as PMID:17637780; one dataset can count two or three times in one statement.
P23468's function text is ECO:0000250 from UniProtKB Q64487 (crossSpecies), but the quoted span is not marked 'By similarity' and the source species is not in the text, so no taxon can be set.
No term for an animal-model analogue phenotype ('RLS-like motor behaviour'); I used HP:0012452 Restless legs, whose definition (an irresistible urge) a mouse cannot report.
One STRING edge (combined 0.45, experimental 0.41, which the run calls the weakest in its network) makes 'BTBD9 binds ACO1' established (belief 0.8), the same as a UniProt function sentence.

One GWAS row with 116,647 cases at p = 1e-688 leaves 'rs10947738-A raises RLS risk' at belief 0.5 (unsupported), while a single review sentence about a disease feature gives H1.5's associations 0.6; kind weighting ignores sample size and p-value.

One MGI annotation of a mouse genotype (curatedDb) makes S3, S4, S25 and S26 established (0.8) although taxonConsistent is false, while S2's primary zebrafish knockout paper (mechanistic) stays unsupported at 0.7; the database row outranks the experiment it summarises.
I merged 'PTPRD locus variation' and 'PTPRD pleiotropy' into PTPRD: a gene-level association is variation at the locus, and a BLN variant class with no direction would add nothing.
